title: On the notion of a patterning property in model theory
summary: Different kinds of definable patterns in the models of a first-order theory, such as the order property, the tree property, or the ($n$-)strict order property, allow us to distinguish theories according to their logical complexity. The complexity distinctions given by these definable patterns play a central role in model theory. However, a rigorous definition of the notion of a model-theoretic patterning property has yet to be established.
